methodology: Historical incidents reconstructed from primary dated statements and filings. Evidence published after an incident is retrospective; no historical hazard-map snapshot has been verified for predictive backtesting.

cases.title: Baxter North Cove — Hurricane Helene flooding
cases.summary: Severe flooding damaged North Cove assets and stopped production. The plant was fully operational by the end of Q1 2025, with supply recovery efforts extending beyond the immediate event.
cases.pre_event_evidence_status: No historically versioned, site-verified pre-September 2024 flood-zone assessment has yet been confirmed in this application.
cases.financial_effect: 2024 pre-tax net charges of $110 million: $44 million asset/inventory write-offs plus $317 million other costs, offset by $251 million insurance recoveries. Separately, 2025 pre-tax net charges of $133 million disclosed later; do not mix event-period and filing-period figures.
cases.resilience: Company-managed product allocations, outside manufacturing capacity and temporary import arrangements during recovery.

milestones.fact: Hurricane Helene flooding affected the North Cove site; production temporarily stopped.
milestones.note: This report confirms historical damage but was not pre-event evidence.

milestones.fact: Company reported FDA coordination, allocation restrictions and mitigation using other sites and temporary imports.
milestones.note: Operational contingency action, not a loss forecast.

milestones.fact: Baxter reported that the North Cove plant was fully operational by the end of first-quarter 2025.
milestones.note: Reporting date is not the publication date; disclosure filed later.

milestones.fact: 2025 annual filing separately disclosed $110 million 2024 net charges and $133 million 2025 net charges, and insurance recovery components for 2024.
milestones.note: 2024 and 2025 accounting figures are distinct years, not insured claim totals.

underwriting.property_damage: Observed: flood-related damage to manufacturing assets and inventory. Present-day flood zone not yet verified.
underwriting.business_interruption: Observed: production closure and extended restoration; revenue value and policy attachment unknown.
underwriting.environmental_liability: No facility-specific pollution loss established by these storm disclosures.
underwriting.supply_chain: Observed: IV solutions constraints; allocations, alternative capacity and FDA coordination.
underwriting.resilience: Observed: phased recovery and alternate capacity. Engineer-verified defenses and protection elevations unknown.

cases.title: Pfizer Rocky Mount — July 2023 tornado
cases.outcome: Confirmed physical damage and staged manufacturing restart
cases.summary: A tornado severely damaged the site's large warehouse and affected sterile injectables supply. Most lines restarted in September 2023, but supply constraints persisted into 2024.
cases.pre_event_evidence_status: No verified pre-July 2023 site-specific tornado-exposure assessment or engineering vulnerability document has been imported.
cases.financial_effect: Pfizer disclosed losses partially offset by insurance recoveries, but this research does not attribute a defensible total insured loss to the specific site.
cases.resilience: Phased recovery, emergency ordering, temporary warehousing, quality assurance, product transfers to other manufacturing sites.

milestones.fact: Pfizer confirmed tornado damage, mainly affecting the HiRise warehouse; FDA evaluated medicine-supply consequences.
milestones.note: Manufacturer statement made after the tornado.

milestones.fact: FDA said no immediate significant supply effect was anticipated, but continued monitoring and inventory assessment were necessary.
milestones.note: Initial agency assessment, not a definitive conclusion about later supply.

milestones.fact: Pfizer reported the majority of manufacturing lines restarted; full supply of some medicines could be affected until at least mid-2024.
milestones.note: Full manufacturing restart is not equivalent to full supply restoration.

milestones.fact: Health Canada reported commercial production had resumed for all affected products and deliveries to Canada had begun.
milestones.note: Country-specific supply update; not a complete loss valuation.

underwriting.property_damage: Observed: damaged warehouse and stored materials. Roof and structural engineering details unavailable.
underwriting.business_interruption: Observed: staged production restart, followed by delayed supply recovery.
underwriting.environmental_liability: No pollution-loss conclusion supported by these tornado records.
underwriting.supply_chain: Observed: sterile injectable supply dependencies; temporary product/warehouse substitutions.
underwriting.resilience: Observed: alternate warehousing, manufacturing tech transfers and emergency-order management.

cases.title: Amgen Juncos — Hurricane Maria resilience
cases.outcome: Some site damage; uninterrupted patient supply reported
cases.summary: Hurricane Maria damaged island infrastructure and caused some site damage, but critical manufacturing areas were not significantly impacted and the company reported uninterrupted medicine supply. Temporary operating measures included generators and water reserves.
cases.pre_event_evidence_status: The site had standing contingency resources, but the public sources reviewed here do not establish which planning details or hurricane models were independently available before the storm.
cases.financial_effect: No attributable insured site loss amount established in this case study. Do not treat broader 2017 company restructuring charges as hurricane loss.
cases.resilience: Backup diesel generation, pre-arranged fuel deliveries, storage tanks/wells, satellite or microwave links, international manufacturing capacity and maintained inventory.

milestones.fact: Amgen reported critical Juncos manufacturing areas not significantly impacted, no lost finished or in-process inventory and power from backup generators.
milestones.note: Post-storm update, not a pre-event probability estimate.

milestones.fact: Amgen described fuel contracts, backup water supply, alternate connectivity and gradual restart of production while maintaining worldwide medicine supply.
milestones.note: Date approximate; article date not independently verified.

milestones.fact: Drug-substance and packaging plants were fully operational; formulation/filling recovery remained underway, with uninterrupted patient supply reported.
2017 Form 10-K said diesel generators supplied the facility through 2017 and grid power returned in January 2018.
milestones.note: Approximate restoration month; not a specific January 1 event.

underwriting.property_damage: Some physical damage reported; critical manufacturing areas not significantly affected.
underwriting.business_interruption: Restoration of manufacturing activity occurred, but Amgen reported no interruption to global patient supply.
underwriting.environmental_liability: No site-specific pollution loss established by the reviewed storm disclosures.
underwriting.supply_chain: Observed: exposure to island-wide power, fuel and water continuity; inventory buffered patient supply.
underwriting.resilience: Documented generators, fuel contracts, water storage/wells, alternative communications and global capacity.
